rationale: Edge-case lens ran clean; acceptance did not run because no story/spec ArtifactRef exists for this branch (genuine no-spec, forces confidence low). 2 of 4 edge-case candidates verified as dismissible (pytest-cov auto-combines coverage data under xdist; breakpoint/debugger friction under -n is a dev-convenience concern below the blocking floor), 2 kept as patch findings after reading the real files. Standards audit ran with no coverage gap but reported 1 blocking commit-format violation (4/8 commits in range carry no EPMCDME ticket prefix), confirmed against git log. 0 findings deferred, 2 dismissed as noise.

standards_review.notes: 4 of 8 commit subjects in range carry no ticket prefix; other 4 use placeholder ticket EPMCDME-0000.
No Python source changed; Ruff/typing rules and license-header check do not apply to Dockerfile/Makefile/pytest.ini/poetry.lock.
No auth/secrets/untrusted-input surface touched; Dockerfile chmod reorder and nemo-switchyard PyPI switch are security-neutral-to-positive.

findings.title: Venv read-only mode not re-verified after COPY
findings.problem: chmod 555 is applied to $VIRTUAL_ENV once in the builder stage (line 38); production (line 55) relies solely on COPY --from=builder to carry that mode forward, per the rationale comment at lines 53-54, with no explicit check that the mode survived the cross-stage copy.
findings.impact: If the build backend ever fails to preserve source mode bits on a cross-stage COPY, the production image's virtualenv silently loses its read-only defense-in-depth with no build-time signal; this repo has no way to execute Docker to confirm COPY --from mode-preservation on the actual build path, so the risk is real but unconfirmed rather than dismissed.
findings.recommendation: Add a build-time assertion in the production stage (e.g. `RUN test "$(stat -c %a \"$VIRTUAL_ENV\")" = "555"`) or reapply `chmod 555` in the production stage as defense-in-depth so a silent permission regression fails the build instead of shipping.

findings.title: Commit subjects missing ticket prefix
findings.problem: git-workflow.md requires commit subjects in the form 'EPMCDME-####: Description'; 4 of the 8 commits in this range (f3b2750a4, c7424561d, 19d20ecd9, dd7daf443) carry no ticket prefix at all, confirmed against `git log main..HEAD`.
findings.impact: git-workflow.md is a documented blocking standard for this repo; non-conforming commit subjects fail the repo's own commit-format gate.
findings.recommendation: Reword the affected commits (or the squash-merge commit message) to lead with the ticket prefix, e.g. 'EPMCDME-0000: Drop redundant -n auto --maxprocesses=6 from Makefile test/coverage targets'.

findings.title: No xdist fallback for restricted CI runners
findings.problem: addopts now hardcodes `-n 2` for every pytest invocation (confirmed: no env-var override or `-p no:xdist` fallback exists anywhere in pytest.ini, Makefile, or .gitlab-ci.yml, which has no pytest step at all — the external CI job referenced in commit c7424561d lives outside this repo).
findings.impact: In a restricted runner that cannot spawn xdist worker subprocesses, the entire pytest invocation would error out rather than degrade to serial execution; whether the external CI job actually imposes such a restriction could not be confirmed from this repo, so this is an ambiguous, newly-introduced risk rather than a confirmed break.
findings.recommendation: Document (and ideally wire, e.g. via a supported `PYTEST_ADDOPTS="-p no:xdist"` override) a way to disable xdist for restricted runners and local interactive debugging, so the `-n 2` default degrades gracefully instead of hard-failing.
